Normalisation factor of each sample

Source: R/fct_viz.R
draw_normalisation_factors.Rd

How far normalisation had to move each sample to make it comparable to the others. A factor near 1 means the library needed almost no correction ; one far from it means a skewed composition, where a small number of genes take a large share of the reads.

This is what changes between raw and normalised counts. The sequencing depth itself does not, see draw_sequencing_depth.

draw_normalisation_factors(
  tcc,
  k = 5,
  delta = 0.05,
  palette = getOption("DIANE.palette", "ggplot")
)

Arguments

tcc

a TCC object, as returned by normalize.

k

number of median absolute deviations from the median beyond which a sample is flagged.

delta

minimal deviation from the median, as a fraction of it. A sample must exceed both thresholds to be flagged.

palette

categorical palette : "ggplot", "diane", "okabe", "npg", "aaas", "lancet" or "nejm". Defaults to getOption("DIANE.palette"), else "ggplot".

Value

a ggplot object

Examples

data("abiotic_stresses")
tcc <- DIANE::normalize(abiotic_stresses$raw_counts,
                        abiotic_stresses$conditions, iteration = FALSE)
draw_normalisation_factors(tcc)
